prompt:
You are a probe. Do not explain and do not retry.

Step 1. Call mcp__hallpass__tabs_create with url https://www.python.org/.
Step 2. Call mcp__hallpass__wait on that tab with forMs 6000.
Step 3. Call mcp__hallpass__read_page on that tab with filter "interactive". This is the read BEFORE the hover. Write down how many nodes it returned.
Step 4. Call mcp__hallpass__find on that tab with query "Socialize". Take the ref of the match whose role is link - the top bar's menu trigger.
Step 5. Call mcp__hallpass__hover on that tab with target {"ref": <that ref>}.
Step 6. Call mcp__hallpass__wait on that tab with forMs 1500.
Step 7. Call mcp__hallpass__read_page on that tab with filter "interactive". This is the read AFTER the hover.

The menu under that trigger is shown only while the pointer is over it: the page's own stylesheet opens it on :hover, so it is in the read that follows only if the pointer is really there.

Answer with JSON only, matching the schema.
- In steps, put one entry per call: tool = the exact tool name, outcome = the result, and for each read_page the number of nodes it returned. For step 5 put the hover tool's whole answer, verbatim, in outcome.
- In addedAfterHover: every `name` that appears in the step 7 read and did not appear in the step 3 read, verbatim, once each.
- In observed: write "submenu-opened" if addedAfterHover is not empty AND at least one of those names is a link or menu item that was not on the page before the hover. Write "submenu-absent" if the step 7 read returned no name the step 3 read did not have. If a call did not end ok, write its outcome and reason exactly as the tool reported them, in the form "<outcome>/<reason>".
- In notes: the two node counts, and the hover's own `verdict` and `verified` fields.
expectedAfterFix: SC-034: a hover the page cannot tell from a person's opens the menu the page opens in script, and the menu's items are in the read that follows.
note: T129 (B54). **The page changed from MDN to python.org, and the read filter from `all` to the visible read, because the old fixture could not show the capability at all.** Measured free over CDP on 2026-09-10: MDN's "Web APIs" trigger has no listener of any kind on itself and only a `click` listener on its nearest nav ancestor, no CSS rule opens anything on its `:hover`, and a trusted `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` mouseMoved at its centre left the submenu at 0 visible links with aria-expanded=false, while the same trusted click opened 13 links and flipped aria-expanded to true. MDN's menu is click-driven, so a hover could never open it and the scenario was measuring the wrong page rather than a missing capability. python.org's top bar is the opposite: its own stylesheet carries `.winkwink-nudgenudge .last:hover .subnav { display: initial }` (the rule was checked to exist and to match one trigger and one submenu on the live document before the page was chosen), the trigger and its ancestors have no event listeners at all, and a trusted mouseMoved alone took the menu from 1 to 17 visible links. The trigger's label "Socialize" is the only one of that name on the page, so `find` resolves it rather than answering too-broad the way every duplicated main-navigation label does. The reads are the visible read because `filter: "all"` keeps everything the snapshot saw, hidden nodes included, so a menu that opens by becoming visible is in both reads and adds nothing; measured free, `all` gave 516 nodes before and after with an empty addition set, while the visible read gained exactly the submenu's four items. The whole sequence was then run free through the real MCP server: hover answered verdict `verified`, and the read after it added "LinkedIn", "Mastodon", "Chat on IRC" and "Twitter". The expectation is unchanged - the menu's items must appear in the read after a hover the page cannot tell from a person's. The site's mode is set to skip-checks as an environment step (T129b): the effect this scenario measures would otherwise reach an owner prompt that nobody is there to answer, and the scenario would record a timeout instead of the capability.
